text:
Toronto has lost four straight, been outscored 17-7, and earned only 42% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in those games. At 8-10-2 the Leafs have an 8% chance at the playoffs in our simulations, tied for the lowest of any team in this group, and the headlines have turned. Auston Matthews calling out teammates after the loss to New Jersey, pieces on his trade value, and rumor columns already running Brad Treliving, Craig Berube and Joel Quenneville in the same breath.

The scary part is that the scoreboard has been kind. Toronto has scored seven more goals than its chances deserved and still sits below .500. Season-long it gets 47% of the chances, and 46% at five on five. Sergei Bobrovsky is 0-5-0 with an .857 save percentage over his last five starts.

There is one line working. Jack Roslovic, Matthews and Easton Cowan get 58% of the chances and have outscored teams 9-2, and Roslovic has 14 points in his last 10 games against 7.7 expected. It will cool. The top pair, Jake McCabe and Darren Raddysh, gets only 44% of the chances, and Chris Tanev has said he doesn't agree with the plan to manage his workload.

Gavin McKenna's rookie growing pains are part of this, and a call-up for Ryan Tverberg to skate with John Tavares and William Nylander says the coaches are searching. What to watch: whether anything changes behind the bench before the standings make the decision for them.
headline: The Leafs are spiralling, and it's real
